notes:
Summary: Large healthcare analytics shop building clinician-assistant + clinical summarization pipelines. Wants predictable reserved capacity for production inference (PHI in scope). Primary ask: sizing workshop followed by a Dedicated reservation quote and HIPAA addendum.

Workload details (from questionnaire + calls):
- Primary workload: clinician assistant chat (multi-turn), clinical note summarization (batch nightly), semantic search (embeddings) for EHR retrieval.
- Steady-state: ~180 QPS average across regions (N. America), token profile ~45 tokens/request average (short chats) -> ~8k tokens/sec steady.
- Peak bursts: up to 1,200 QPS for 60-90s during morning triage windows; token/sec peak ~100k tokens/sec.
- Typical request size: 8-120 tokens (longer summarization jobs batched).
- Latency goals: p95 < 250ms for chat generation (short responses), p99 < 700ms preferred; willing to accept higher p99 for long summary jobs if batched.
- Throughput/guarantee ask: committed baseline throughput for 200 QPS with burst capacity to 1,000 QPS; automatic fallback to smaller quantized model on overload.
- Durability/security: colocated KMS, audit logs retention 7 years, SSO/SAML + SCIM, SOC2 + HIPAA BAAs required.

Sizing hints collected so far (for workshop):
- Model family: open Llama-derivative 13B quantized for chat; optionally 70B for high-fidelity summarization (batch window).
- Target GPU profile: mix of GPU types — a pool of 8x A10/A6000-equivalent for steady-state + 4x A100-style for bursty/high-capacity summarization during nightly windows OR a reserved 12-GPU pool with autoscale buffer.
- Batching/backpressure: recommend request-level batching for nightly summarization + continuous KV caching for chat to save token compute.

SLA/Commercial notes:
- Client pushes for SLA: 99.95% uptime and explicit throughput guarantees during business hours (07:00-19:00 UTC-8). Wants credit formula tied to p99 latency breaches.
- Procurement: Legal and Security need HIPAA addendum + data residency clause. Budget committee to approve capex for reserved plan in May.
- Quote sensitivity: flexible on model quantization if unit cost drops 15-25%; wants clear unit economics scenario modeling.

Direct quote from head of platform: "We need predictable ops cost — if your reserved plan can guarantee latency under load and a clean HIPAA pathway, we can sign a multi-year commitment."

Next recommended steps (workshop deliverables):
1) 2-hour remote sizing workshop (engineer + SE + AE) to validate QPS/token profiles and agree fallback policies.
2) Redwood to produce: GPU pool sketch (counts by SKU), expected p95/p99 latency ranges per workload, estimated monthly unit cost, failover routing plan, and draft SLA language for throughput credits.
3) Run 2-week POC on Dedicated with representative traffic replay (billing cap applied) and run the regression eval suite.

Notes/FAQ stubs referenced: drive:Zenith/Redwood-dedicated-pricing-v1.pdf, drive:Zenith/hipaa-questionnaire.xlsx. Jira RINF-4521 tracking HIPAA integration questions.
